faq.q: What is the origin of Hanin?
faq.a: Hanin is associated with Arabic. Hanin is Arabic حَنِين (Ḥanīn) 'longing, yearning, tender attachment', from the root ح ن ن (ḥ-n-n). The word appears in the Qur'an. The source gloss 'grace, charm, kindness' is a loose rendering; 'longing, yearning' is the lexical sense. Same name as haneen.
Yes — the underlying form حنين is Arabic.
Hanin can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.

faq.q: What does Hanin mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Hanin is rendered حنین and carries the sense نرمی، دلکشی، مہربانی.

faq.q: What does Hanin mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Hanin is rendered حنين and carries the sense لطف، دلربایی، مهربانی.
A romanized syllable approximation is ha-nin. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Hanin?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Hanin, hanin. Script forms are حنين, حنین, हनीन.

faq.q: Is Hanin a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
